newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: The Dutch sharemarket dived into negative territory on Friday, finishing lower for the first time in four days but bouncing off the day's lows.
Dealers said mid-afternoon selling of U.S. Treasury bonds and share index futures pushed global markets down but the opening on Wall Street was not as negative as first feared.
"Everybody realised things were not as bad as it seemed (initially)," one dealer said.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares closed at 996.16 points, down 14.81 points or 1.46 percent from Thursday's level, which had been a closing record.
The Dutch index had risen more than 15 points over the week.
Another dealer said an unwinding of long positions in Treasuries on dollar softness undermined global markets.
Most major Dutch stocks finished lower, spearheaded by publisher Elsevier, which shed 2.30 guilders or 6.5 percent to end at 32.90.
In the wake of disappointing results from the Reed/Elsevier group earlier this week, some brokers have downgraded Elsevier to a Hold from a Buy.
Analysts said they preferred rival publisher Wolters Kluwer, which ended off 0.70 at 282.00 guilders.
Royal Dutch Petroleum lost ground for the second successive day, ending down 3.50 at 114.40 guilders, after disappointing second quarter profit figures on Thursday.
Gains shown in morning trading by consumer products group Unilever and chemicals producer Akzo Nobel evaporated as the day proceeded and they ended lower.
Both have reported strong half-year profit figures.
But food group Nutricia went against the flow, closing 6.60 guilders firmer at 363.70.
A trader attributed this to "the fact that they had been hammered in the course of the week".
